questions.q: Which report format does this lesson recommend for Dmitri's view of Installation Jobs grouped by both Technician and Status at once?
options: Tabular
Matrix
Summary
Joined
questions.explain: Matrix reports group by rows and columns at once -- exactly what's needed for Technician (rows) by Status (columns).

questions.q: Why does this lesson say building a custom Apex page for Dmitri's ad hoc questions would be the wrong approach?
options: Apex pages cannot query Installation_Job__c
Apex pages are slower than reports in every case
Reports and Apex pages produce identical output so there's no difference
It would be over-engineering for a question that changes shape depending on who's asking -- exactly what the declarative-first principle warns against
questions.explain: Ad hoc, user-driven questions that vary in shape are the native fit for Report Builder; building custom code for every such question would be the over-engineering Lesson 2's declarative-first principle warns against.

questions.q: What does the custom report type built in this lesson expose that the standard, automatically generated Warranty Claims report type doesn't?
options: The ability to filter by Claim_Status__c
The ability to export to CSV
Fields from related objects -- Case's Subject and Asset's SerialNumber -- as selectable report columns
Access to Apex trigger logic
questions.explain: A custom report type lets a report pull fields from specified related objects (Case, Asset) in addition to the primary object's own fields, which the default report type doesn't expose.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use a bucket field instead of a new formula field on `Warranty_Claim__c` for the Small/Medium/Large grouping?
options: A bucket field creates a report-only grouping with no schema change, appropriate for a temporary reporting need rather than a permanent object change
Formula fields cannot reference Currency fields
Bucket fields are faster to query than formula fields
Claim_Amount__c cannot be used in a formula field
questions.explain: A bucket field groups values into named ranges inside the report itself, with no new field added to the object -- the right fit for a reporting-only need rather than a permanent schema change.

questions.q: Per this lesson, does report folder access override the record-level security from Lesson 4's security model?
options: Yes, anyone who can open a report folder sees all records in it regardless of sharing rules
Report folders replace the need for any object-level security
Report folders only apply to Tabular reports
No -- folder access controls who can see and run a report, but the underlying record-level security (OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules) still applies to what rows actually show
questions.explain: Folder sharing controls visibility of the report itself, not the records it returns -- a user running a report still only sees rows their existing record-level security already permits.
